name: verify-loop
description: Verify Loop: one place to verify a change or claim. It writes a check that can fail, loops until the check passes, keeps the proof, and returns a fixed answer (verdict, VERIFY: line, observed rejection, gaps). Users, skills and agents can all call it. Create mode generates a project /verify skill; maintain mode keeps it honest as the app changes. Also ships feature-map (manual-only): a FEATURES.md of every feature, its entry points and traces, checked against the code and linked to VERIFY.md. And latent-audit (manual-only): a dead-code cleanup held to three stages (a snapshot that records what each command really imports, in-place deletion of only never-loaded code with every command rerun, a verdict for every suspect left). And wire-check (manual-only): is code connected to the running system? A call-trace snapshot of every way in records which functions really ran, every function nothing entered gets a classified verdict, and a component you connect is kept connected by a FEATURES.md trace and a VERIFY.md check seen red on the broken wiring. And debug-protocol (manual-only): the root cause proven both ways, the failure reproduced on demand and gone with only the cause taken out, then the tree left as it was or fixed at the cause and held by a check that fails with the cause put back. And structure-gate (manual-only): is it spaghetti, measured? The share of code a parser actually entered comes first, every region no parser entered (code in a string, a language with no parser here) gets a counted reading or UNKNOWN, every finding gets its cost, and a `no` verdict is refused over code no linter or test can reach. And threat-model (manual-only): what an attacker can make the system do, worst first. A scan counts every way in (route tables, registering decorators, handlers, scripts), each one is attacked or shown to have nothing behind it, and each attack is kept as a test the suite runs; a fix must shut every open attack and fail again with the change put back. The install runs no hooks.
